subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: Should an unavailable Codex native relay remain fail-closed while OpenClaw repairs its descriptor, or may it fall back to generic before-tool-call hooks after proving equivalent enforcement?
rationale: The relay path includes generation-bound and session-aware enforcement that is not automatically equivalent to the generic hook path, so accepting fallback behavior requires explicit security ownership.

options.title: Repair the relay boundary
options.body: Preserve fail-closed behavior and refresh or recreate the descriptor using the current relay generation after gateway restart.

options.title: Approve policy fallback
options.body: Allow generic before-tool-call fallback only after demonstrating parity for loop detection, approval policy, cancellation, and failure handling.

recommendation.title: Repair the relay boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve fail-closed behavior and refresh or recreate the descriptor using the current relay generation after gateway restart.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the merged fallback contract that deliberately distinguished safe no-policy handling from unknown unavailable state.
